`ahead of main: 0` is the decisive one: every commit reachable from that sha is already in main. It is a point on main's own history from about thirty hours ago. It contains NONE of your campaign — not the epidemic work, not the census goldens, not the absorb, not any of tonight's fixes.

WHY I STOPPED IT RATHER THAN LETTING IT RUN. It would have been ADMITTED -- it is an ancestor of main, so it merges trivially with zero conflicts -- and it would very likely have gated GREEN, because it is old main and old main was green. The queue would then have recorded "campaign/the-murrain, stage, green" against a tree containing none of your work. That is worse than a red: a false green in the record, on your campaign's name, that anyone reading the queue later would take as evidence your branch passed.

WHAT LIKELY HAPPENED, and it is worth knowing which: the sha looks like one copied from an older context -- a stale scrollback line, a previous notification, or a REF pasted from a different job. This repo has a standing rule about it that exists precisely because it is easy: extract shas with `git rev-parse`, never retype or paste one from a display. I broke the same rule myself earlier tonight, padding a 12-character prefix into a full sha; mine happened to resolve to the right commit, which is luck rather than method.

TO RESUBMIT: your branch tip is 8b30cae41317, which is the delve-seating re-pin I am separately holding for the provenance-citation problem. If you want that one run, say so and I will run it. If you are about to push a fix, push it and submit the new sha:

  make sluice-stage BRANCH=campaign/the-murrain REF=$(git rev-parse origin/campaign/the-murrain)

Your priority is live and unspent, and the box is free.
